selected_primary_idea.title: DeepBio Census: A Pressure-Preserved Habitat-Resolved Inventory
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Marine deep-biosphere habitat strata across water column, sediment/pore water, and oceanic crustal fluids
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: Energy-redox habitat stratification and cross-platform calibration explain deep-biosphere abundance and activity more faithfully than depth-only extrapolation.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: A hierarchical observation model separates latent living cells, functional potential, realized redox rate, method bias, and contamination.
falsification_conditions: Energy-redox stratification does not improve held-out prediction relative to depth-only baselines.
Independent count, lipid, and molecular channels remain mutually inconsistent outside modeled uncertainty.

rejected_ideas.title: DNA-only global inventory
rejected_ideas.reason: Does not identify living-cell abundance or realized flux.

rejected_ideas.title: Cell-count multiplier for climate impact
rejected_ideas.reason: Standing abundance is not a rate measurement.

rejected_ideas.title: Extraterrestrial-life conclusion
rejected_ideas.reason: Earth analogues support habitability hypotheses only.

mcts_evolution_summary.finding: Depth-only framing collapses distinct compartments and confounds pressure, temperature, and energy supply.
A multiomics atlas requires independent activity and contamination constraints.
A hierarchical census preserves heterogeneous habitats while enabling uncertainty-aware global integration.
